mutant.description: Every limb verdict in this cell is an EQUALITY or an ABSENCE, and both read identically to an instrument that is looking at nothing, so no limb was believed on its own report. FIVE planted-mutation controls ran: on the AST comparator that grades limbs 2 and 4 (build_pack on the deployed side, build_pack on the fresh side, _case_currency and _model_case_line at a631ba6249), and on the pdf comparator that grades limb 5. A sixth control sat on the git plane, where a mangled MSYS ref returns clean-empty and would have made the a631ba6249 baseline read as ABSENT.
mutant.expected: A comparator reporting IDENTICAL must report MOVED when a change is planted inside the very function it just called identical; a git read returning bytes must sit beside a non-resolving read at the same ref that fails loudly rather than returning empty.
mutant.observed: All five planted mutations FIRED -- build_pack on both the deployed and the fresh copy, _case_currency, _model_case_line, and the pdf comparator on a differing content-stream digest. The git control returned rc=128 'path does not exist in a631ba6249' with 0 bytes against 52155 bytes for the real read, so the baseline is a real read and not a mangle. No verdict in this cell rests on an unexercised instrument.

determinism.description: Two things had to be stable for this cell's evidence to mean anything. (a) THE ARTIFACT: the closure diff was graded on a --build-only zip, but a SECOND build produced the bytes that actually shipped, so the two builds had to agree or the graded bytes were not the deployed bytes and limbs 1-4 would have graded something nobody deployed. (b) THE PDF ORACLE: limb 5 grades /print pdf output before and after, and a served pdf's raw sha is known to move per request on /CreationDate, which would make every after-capture read as MOVED.
determinism.expected: (a) The uploaded object's content-sha256 must equal the sha of the graded --build-only zip. (b) Two captures of one key against one unchanged deployment must agree on the content-stream digest, or limb 5 cannot be graded with it at all.
determinism.observed: (a) IDENTICAL: the graded --build-only zip is sha256(b64) LK9h47juBfZPaAyfztAxDe9z65W2ZtEw6H2IJ/DcO4s= at 857326 bytes, and the uploaded object's content-sha256 is LK9h47juBfZPaAyfztAxDe9z65W2ZtEw6H2IJ/DcO4s= at 857326 bytes. The build is deterministic and the graded bytes are the shipped bytes. (b) STABLE: two BA_US_Equity captures agreed on the content-stream digest in the before pass and again in the after pass. The banked /CreationDate hazard did NOT materialise on this renderer -- the raw pdf sha was stable across repeat captures too -- so limb 5 was graded on the raw digest AND the content-stream digest, which is stronger than the limb requires. That is a property of this renderer measured today, not a general claim about served pdfs.
